claim_boundary.supported_after_phase_1: A single external participant prospectively authored and locked initial requests for project-authored controlled scenarios.

participant_instructions: Read the complete scenario card before writing.
Write the first message you would naturally send to an assistant.
Use your own wording; do not copy the private goal sentence.
Do not deliberately make the request easier or harder for the assistant.
Do not include intent labels, research categories, credentials, or real private information.
It is acceptable not to mention every fact initially if that is how you would naturally ask.
If you genuinely cannot form a request, use the unable-to-respond option instead of inventing one.

assistant_policy_contract.role: A sandboxed planning assistant operating without real-world authority.
assistant_policy_contract.semantic_authority: The assistant may propose interpretations but may not see participant-private goals or constraints.
assistant_policy_contract.execution_boundary: No purchases, messages, account changes, bookings, or physical actions may occur.

participant_card.setting: You are planning groceries for two people for four evening meals this week.
participant_card.private_goal: Create an affordable grocery list whose ingredients can be reused across the four meals without making every meal feel the same.
known_facts: Your total budget is about $70.
The meals must be vegetarian.
One person has a serious peanut allergy.
You already have rice, canned tomatoes, olive oil, and common dried spices.
You are happy to eat leftovers once, but not four nights in a row.

participant_card.setting: You are choosing an outfit for a semi-formal garden wedding that begins in the late afternoon and continues outdoors after dark.
participant_card.private_goal: Choose an outfit that is appropriate for the event, warm enough after sunset, comfortable on grass, and assembled only from the listed wardrobe.
known_facts: The temperature is expected to fall to about 8°C in the evening.
You do not wear heels.
Your available main pieces are a navy jumpsuit, a green midi dress, black trousers, and a cream blouse.
You also have a charcoal cardigan, a light tan coat, black flats, and ankle boots.
You do not want to buy anything new.

available_support: ask about the event or preferences
assemble an outfit from disclosed items

participant_card.setting: You are coordinating a free neighbourhood movie night scheduled to begin outdoors at 7:30 PM.
participant_card.private_goal: Choose a practical plan that avoids damaging equipment, gives attendees timely notice, and preserves the event if reasonably possible.
known_facts: The forecast currently gives a 60% chance of rain after 8 PM.
The projector and speakers are not weatherproof.
A nearby community hall is available, but it holds fewer people.
You must decide whether to reserve the hall by 3 PM.
Many attendees will travel by public transit.

available_support: draft a notice without sending it

scenarios.title: Get your aunt to the appointment

participant_card.setting: Your aunt has a medical appointment downtown at 9:30 AM on Monday, and you are helping with transportation rather than medical decisions.
participant_card.private_goal: Find a reliable travel plan that gets her there on time without requiring stairs or exceeding the available transportation budget.
known_facts: She cannot safely use stairs.
The elevator at the nearest subway station is reported out of service.
A direct rideshare is usually about $34.
The available transportation budget is $25.
A family friend with a car is unavailable before 9 AM.
The clinic asks patients to arrive 15 minutes early.

available_support: ask about mobility or timing constraints

scenarios.title: Ask for the folding table back

participant_card.setting: A neighbour borrowed your folding table several weeks ago. You need it for a family gathering this Saturday.
participant_card.private_goal: Ask for the table back clearly and kindly while preserving the relationship and preparing a backup if the neighbour cannot return it in time.
known_facts: The neighbour has recently been recovering from an illness.
They did not respond to a casual message you sent three days ago.
You do not want to imply that they are dishonest or inconsiderate.
You need a definite answer by Thursday evening.

available_support: draft a message without sending it

participant_card.setting: A close friend has cancelled plans with you at the last minute twice. You are hurt, but you do not know why it happened.
participant_card.private_goal: Begin an honest conversation that communicates the impact on you without assuming your friend acted maliciously or demanding an immediate explanation.
known_facts: You value the friendship and want to preserve it.
You have a trip planned together next month and want to address the issue beforehand.
Your friend has seemed stressed recently but has not explained why.
You prefer a short message that opens a conversation rather than a long confrontation by text.

available_support: draft a message without sending it

participant_card.setting: A coworker you like but do not know closely has lost a parent. You want to acknowledge the loss.
participant_card.private_goal: Write a brief, caring message that does not pressure the coworker to respond and does not make assumptions about their beliefs or relationship with the deceased.
known_facts: You learned about the death through your manager.
You do not know the coworker’s religious beliefs.
You can offer to cover one routine work task next week.
You want to avoid clichés and unsolicited advice.

available_support: ask about the relationship or available support
draft a message without sending it

participant_card.setting: Your church community is arranging meals for a family with a new baby.
participant_card.private_goal: Create a simple volunteer rota that meets the family’s food and privacy needs without overwhelming them with messages or deliveries.
known_facts: The family requested vegetarian meals and no mushrooms.
Deliveries should be left at the door between 5 and 7 PM.
They asked not to have their address posted in the general group chat.
Ten volunteers have offered to help over two weeks.
The family would prefer meals every other day rather than daily.

available_support: ask about schedule or privacy requirements
draft volunteer instructions without sending them

participant_card.setting: You are leading a 35-minute small-group discussion on the parable of the Good Samaritan in Luke 10:25–37.
participant_card.private_goal: Create an accessible discussion plan focused on mercy and neighbour-love that welcomes both experienced Christians and people unfamiliar with the Bible.
known_facts: The group includes teenagers and adults.
Several attendees are new to Christian language.
You want the passage read aloud before discussion.
You want open questions rather than a lecture.
You do not want the plan to pretend that every interpretive or denominational question has one uncontested answer.

scenarios.title: Explain why Christians disagree about baptism

participant_card.setting: A thoughtful twelve-year-old relative has noticed that Christians in different churches practise baptism differently.
participant_card.private_goal: Give an age-appropriate and fair explanation of several major Christian approaches without declaring one tradition obviously correct.
known_facts: Your family attends an Anglican church.
The child’s close friend attends a Baptist church.
The child specifically asked why some babies are baptized and some people wait until they are older.
You want the answer to distinguish description from endorsement.
You would like the child to feel comfortable asking their own church leaders follow-up questions.

assistant_visible_context.domain: comparative Christian theology for a young audience
available_support: ask about audience or desired depth

participant_card.setting: You are designing a short animated scene in which a character discovers a hidden door.
participant_card.private_goal: Produce a clear storyboard structure where the audience notices a visual clue shortly before the character understands it.
known_facts: The scene must be approximately 30 seconds long.
There can be no spoken dialogue or written exposition.
The storyboard may contain no more than eight shots.
The hidden door is revealed by a moving patch of light.
The character should feel cautious rather than frightened.

participant_card.setting: You want to turn an unused corner of a rented apartment into a comfortable reading area.
participant_card.private_goal: Create a warm, practical reading corner within budget without drilling holes or introducing items unsafe for the resident cat.
known_facts: The total budget is $150.
The corner is about one metre wide and is beside an electrical outlet.
The lease does not permit drilling or permanent fixtures.
A curious cat chews exposed cords and knocks over unstable objects.
You already own a comfortable chair but need light and small-item storage.

available_support: ask about space, budget, or preferences

participant_card.setting: In a fictional wizard’s tower, you need to reach the observatory and return safely with the moon key.
participant_card.private_goal: Find a route to the observatory that retrieves the moon key without waking the sleeping guardian on the floor below.
known_facts: A glass stair appears only while a blue rune is active.
The blue rune fades after three actions.
Fire magic or ringing bells will wake the guardian.
A frost charm can keep the glass stair solid for one additional action.
The moon key is kept in a silver cabinet in the observatory.
You have a frost charm, a lantern, and a silent opening spell.

available_support: ask about fictional rules or inventory
check a plan against disclosed rules

scenarios.title: Why did the town clock stop?

participant_card.setting: In a pretend clockwork village, the town clock stopped exactly at noon. The mayor wants an investigation before anyone attempts a repair.
participant_card.private_goal: Propose a fair evidence-gathering sequence that identifies the most likely mechanical cause without prematurely accusing anyone of sabotage.
known_facts: The weather was calm when the clock stopped.
The baker heard one sharp metallic click shortly before noon.
An apprentice adjusted the clock’s minute hand the previous day.
The winding key is still locked in the tower cabinet.
A maintenance log and the clock mechanism can both be inspected.
There is currently no direct evidence of deliberate damage.

scenarios.title: Power choices during the lunar dust storm

participant_card.setting: In a fictional lunar settlement, an incoming dust storm will reduce available solar power for one night.
participant_card.private_goal: Allocate the settlement’s limited stored power so that essential safety needs are met and an important message can be sent if feasible.
known_facts: Six power units are available for the entire night.
Habitat heating requires three units and is essential.
The greenhouse requires two units to prevent crop loss.
The long-range transmitter requires two units to send a scheduled medical-supply request.
A local celebration would require one unit but can be postponed without material harm.
The transmitter and greenhouse do not need to run at the same time, but each consumes its full allocation once used.

participant_card.setting: A local library has received a box of partly labelled family photographs for a small community-history exhibition.
participant_card.private_goal: Create a careful two-week workflow for identifying and selecting photographs without presenting uncertain identities as facts or violating a family member’s privacy request.
known_facts: Dates on the photographs are approximate and several names conflict.
The donor can answer questions but is only available once next week.
Local newspaper archives can be searched.
One living family member asked not to have childhood photographs displayed.
The exhibition can label uncertain information explicitly.
The final display has room for twelve photographs.
